two differences, and only one of them is explained. (1) The handle: theirs takes `rclc_lifecycle_node_t*`, ours `rcl_lifecycle_state_machine_t*` -- one handle instead of two, see `c:lifecycle_node_t`. (2) The trailing `bool publish_update`, which rclc threads into every `rcl_lifecycle_trigger_transition_by_id` call, selects whether the transition is announced on `~/transition_event`. REP-2002's *communication interface* is the five services PLUS a `lifecycle_msgs/msg/TransitionEvent` publisher on `~/transition_event`. We ship the services and **no transition_event publisher at all** -- grep the tree: the type appears only in a round-trip unit test. A supervisor therefore cannot watch our transitions passively; it has to poll `~/get_state`. Nobody decided this, so it is a gap, not a decline. Phase 379 W3. STILL OPEN after phase-417 W4.f, which closed the other fourteen lifecycle gaps and left this one deliberately: the other half of the row -- `cpp:LifecyclePublisher` and the managed-entity protocol it named as the same missing piece -- is CLOSED, so what remains is specifically the publisher on the wire.

The `bool publish_update` argument follows the publisher and is not the work. Its own item, not a rider on a C++ header wave. The handle half of the row is separately settled at `c:lifecycle_node_t` (`divergence`) and is not reopened here.

RE-READ (phase-444 gap re-read, 2026-09-23) — KEPT, and this is the one row in the eight-shard re-read whose reason needed no correction. Re-measured: `git grep TransitionEvent -- packages` returns `nros-node/src/lifecycle_services.rs:901` (the `round_trip_transition_event` unit test), the generated `nros-lifecycle-msgs` crate, and two schema/size test tables — no publisher, and the string `transition_event` appears as a TOPIC nowhere. The correlator still scores the row `differs` (ours arity 2, theirs 3), which is the `publish_update` argument.

CLOSED 2026-10-01 (issue 1587) — the publisher SHIPPED, and the study's price for it was wrong in the direction that mattered. `register_lifecycle_services` now creates a `lifecycle_msgs/msg/TransitionEvent` publisher on `~/transition_event` beside the five servers, `LifecyclePollingNodeCtx::trigger_transition` records every transition it performs, and the executor drains the record onto the wire during `spin_once`. Recording at the state machine rather than at each caller is what makes `ros2 lifecycle set`, `rclc_executor_lifecycle_change_state`, `nros_cpp_lifecycle_change_state`, `nros_cpp_lifecycle_autostart` and the safe `LifecycleCallbacks` road all announce without any of them being told to. A supervisor can watch passively; the `~/get_state` poll is no longer the only way.

THE QoS, MEASURED, AND IT REFUTES THE STUDY. phase-467 §"Row 9" priced this as the most expensive of its thirteen rows on the premise that `~/transition_event` is TRANSIENT_LOCAL — and a transient-local publisher declares a zenoh CACHE QUERYABLE (issue 1378) against a `ZPICO_MAX_QUERYABLES` that defaults to 8 embedded while `[param_services]` (6) and `[lifecycle]` (5) already claim eleven (issue 0460), so a sixth lifecycle slot is the difference between an image that boots and one that dies in `ServiceServerCreationFailed`. Measured twice (2026-09-29, 2026-10-01) against a live `ros2 run lifecycle lifecycle_talker` on humble: `ros2 topic info -v /lc_talker/transition_event` reports RELIABLE / VOLATILE / Infinite lifespan — i.e. `rmw_qos_profile_default`, which `rcl_lifecycle`'s `rcl_lifecycle/src/com_interface.c` takes from `rcl_publisher_get_default_options()` and never overrides. Ours is byte-for-byte that profile. So the price of this row is ONE publisher slot and ONE liveliness token per lifecycle-enabled image and ZERO queryables; `max_queryables`, `tl_publishers`, the retention pool and `nros_sizing_descriptor::transient_local_publishers_over` are all untouched. The expensive half of the row did not exist. Guarded both ends: `the_transition_event_publisher_is_volatile` (nros-node) fails a later switch to transient-local before any board's table does, and `a_lifecycle_image_pays_one_publisher_and_no_queryable` (nros-cli-core) asserts the four pool deltas. `check-infra-queryable-counts` gained a third group holding `LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_PUBLISHERS` to its creation site, because a count with no gate is how the queryable number came to be stated as six twice.

WHAT REMAINS, AND WHY IT IS NOT A GAP. The arity (ours 2, theirs 3) is the trailing `bool publish_update`, and it does not follow the publisher after all. rclc threads it because ITS handle owns the communication interface; `rcl_lifecycle_state_machine_t` is a pure state machine that owns no publisher — the divergence settled at `c:lifecycle_node_t` for a stated platform constraint (static entity storage; the service buffers belong to the entities the executor already owns). On that handle `publish_update` has no referent and could only ever be ignored, and an argument that must be ignored is worse than an absent one. On the EXECUTOR road, where the publisher does live (`c:executor_lifecycle_change_state`), announcement is unconditional, which is what rclcpp does with the flag on every user-facing `change_state`. The handle difference also means the compiler stops a ported call rather than letting it silently differ, so no disposition is carried here — the same posture `c:lifecycle_node_t` takes.
